Where to Stay in Lamphun?
9 Hotels We've Reviewed

heroSub: Nine Lamphun stays across every budget — garden boutique homestays on the edge of town, mid-range hotels and boutiques near town, garden and lakeside resorts, down to old-town hostels by the walking street. Covering the main bases: the old town, Wiang Yong and Pa Sang. Starting from around ฿550–1,050/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right base in Lamphun matter?
introHtml: Lamphun is a small, quiet town right next to Chiang Mai — about a 30–40 minute drive from Chiang Mai's old city — so many travellers use it as a calm base and drive into Chiang Mai for the day. The walled old town is the heart of it — Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, Wat Chamthewi and the Lamphun walking street are all within easy reach. Wiang Yong and Mueang Nga, across the Kuang River, are the newer-stay zone right by town, while Pa Sang and the outskirts suit anyone wanting a quiet garden setting. This guide rounds up 9 Lamphun stays we've picked across every tier — from garden homestays to old-town hostels — each with an honest take from real reviews, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Lamphun has no metro — it's a small town, so a car or motorbike is by far the most practical option, and parking is easy. The walled old town is compact enough to walk Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and the walking street on foot. It's about a 30–40 minute drive from Chiang Mai's old city, and roughly 40 minutes from Chiang Mai Airport. The main bases in this guide: Old town — Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, the walking street · Wiang Yong·Mueang Nga — across the Kuang River, newer stays, near Jamfa · Pa Sang·outskirts — quiet garden settings.

entries.name: Siri Hotel Lumphun
entries.storyHtml: Siri Hotel Lumphun is a mid-range hotel in Wiang Yong with the highest score among the in-town hotels — 9.4 from 113 reviews. The rooms are newly renovated, 25 sqm and tidy, on the Wiang Yong side across the Kuang River close to town, a few minutes' drive to Wat Phra That Hariphunchai. It suits anyone wanting a clean, fresh hotel room on a modest budget as a Lamphun base. Real reviews praise the cleanliness and value.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There are only a couple of room types and the score is high, so book ahead, especially on weekends. The Wiang Yong side drives into town easily and has parking.
pros: 9.4 — highest score among the in-town hotels
Newly renovated 25 sqm rooms, clean and tidy
Wiang Yong location near town, quick to Wat Phra That
Reviews praise cleanliness and value
cons: Only a couple of room types — limited choice
Small hotel, no pool or full resort facilities

entries.name: Loft House Homestay
entries.storyHtml: Loft House Homestay is a budget homestay in the Ban Hong area scoring a high 9.2, starting at just ฿650. Rooms come with AC, Wi-Fi and an en-suite bathroom — clean and simple — and there's a kitchenette room that suits longer stays. It's a quiet little spot for anyone passing through Ban Hong or wanting a budget base in southern Lamphun. Real reviews praise the cleanliness and the hosts' care.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Staying several nights? The kitchenette room is handy. It's out in Ban Hong, so having your own car is the easiest way to get around.
pros: From just ฿650 with AC and a high 9.2 score
Kitchenette room available, good for longer stays
Host-run homestay — reviews praise the welcome
Clean, simple rooms with en-suite bathroom
cons: In the Ban Hong area, a fair way from Lamphun old town

entries.name: Pickbaan Hostel & Cafe
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Lamphun old town · near walking street
tags: 📍 Old town, walk to walking street
entries.addr: Lamphun old town · near the walking street
entries.storyHtml: Pickbaan is a hostel with an in-house cafe in Lamphun's old town, and the most-reviewed stay in this list — 196 reviews, scoring 9.0. The big draw is the old-town location, within walking distance of the walking street and Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, plus a relaxed cafe to hang out in. There are budget dorm beds as well as private rooms for couples or families. Real reviews praise the cafe vibe, the cleanliness, and the walkable old-town setting.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Solo or backpacking? The dorm bed is the cheapest option. Couples or families should take a private room — and the cafe out front is a nice spot for an early coffee before heading out.
pros: Most-reviewed stay in the set, 196 reviews
Old-town location, walk to the walking street and Wat Phra That
In-house cafe with a relaxed vibe
Both budget dorm beds and private rooms
cons: Dorm beds use shared bathrooms — not for those wanting full privacy
It's a hostel, not a full-service hotel

entries.name: GRAND PA Hotel & Resort Lamphun Chiang Mai
entries.addr: Wiang Yong · near Jamfa, Lamphun town
entries.storyHtml: GRAND PA is a newly opened 4-star hotel-resort in the Wiang Yong area, scoring 8.8 from 141 reviews. It's one of the few Lamphun stays with a swimming pool, gym, cafe and bakery on site, with spacious rooms ranging from Deluxe up to a Penthouse Suite. The Wiang Yong location near Jamfa drives into town easily, making it a good pick for families or anyone wanting fuller facilities than a homestay. Real reviews praise the new, spacious rooms and the pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a family or want pool time? This works out better than a homestay. Step up to the Junior Suite for a larger room with a sitting area.
pros: Newly opened 4-star with a swimming pool and gym
In-house cafe and bakery, spacious rooms
Range of room types from Deluxe to Penthouse Suite
Wiang Yong location near Jamfa, easy drive into town
cons: On the Wiang Yong side, not in the old town itself
Priced above the others here — for those wanting fuller facilities

entries.name: Nornlamphun Boutique Hotel
entries.addr: Mueang Nga · near town centre, Lamphun
entries.storyHtml: Nornlamphun is a modern-loft boutique hotel in Mueang Nga near the centre of Lamphun town, scoring 8.6 from 99 reviews. The draw is the clean, exposed-concrete loft design with parquet floors, and the Deluxe rooms add a sitting area and work desk. The location near the centre is a quick drive to Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and the walking street, making it a good pick for design fans on a modest budget. Real reviews praise the design, cleanliness and central location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Standard and Twin rooms are the same ฿900 — pick by group size. Want more space and a work desk? Step up to the Deluxe.
pros: Clean modern-loft design with real character
Mueang Nga location near the centre, quick to the old town
Roomy Deluxe with a sitting area and work desk
Reviews praise cleanliness and value
cons: Small boutique, no pool or full facilities
Standard rooms are compact — choose Deluxe for more space

entries.name: Suksatan @ Lamphun
entries.storyHtml: Suksatan is a boutique resort of Lanna teak bungalows set in a garden, in Umong subdistrict of Mueang Lamphun, scoring 8.5 from 60 reviews. The draw is the Lanna-style wooden bungalows in a quiet garden, with standard cottages and ones built over a pond with a balcony looking onto the water. There's a 2-bedroom house for families, making it a good pick for anyone wanting a Lanna garden-house feel on a modest budget. Real reviews praise the atmosphere, the quiet, and the charm of the teak cottages.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick the bungalow over the pond for the best view and atmosphere. Families get better value from the 2-bedroom house than booking several bungalows.
pros: Lanna teak bungalows in a garden, quiet setting
Bungalows over a pond with a balcony onto the water
2-bedroom house available, good for families
Reviews praise the atmosphere and teak-cottage charm
cons: Wooden cottages in a simple style, not modern hotel rooms
Outside the old town, so your own car helps

entries.name: The Grand Jamjuree Resort Lamphun
entries.storyHtml: The Grand Jamjuree is a resort of cottages set around a pond in a shady garden, in the Mueang Nga area near Lamphun town, scoring 8.4 from 120 reviews. The draw is the cottage rooms scattered around a pond in green grounds, each with a private balcony — quiet, yet a few minutes' drive into town. There's a Triple room for larger groups, making it a good pick for anyone wanting a garden-resort feel on a budget. Real reviews praise the garden, the shade and the quiet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room facing the pond for the best setting. Larger groups get better value from the Triple, and there's parking within the garden.
pros: Cottages around a pond in a shady garden, quiet setting
Every room has a private balcony, near town
Triple room available, good for larger groups
Reviews praise the garden and the shade
cons: An older resort, simple room style rather than modern
On the Mueang Nga side, not in the old town itself

entries.name: BaanKong Hostel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In town · near Wat Phra That Hariphunchai
tags: 📍 In town, near Wat Phra That
entries.addr: Charoen Tha Rd · in Lamphun town
entries.storyHtml: BaanKong is the cheapest stay in this list, from just ฿550, yet it's right in Lamphun town near Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, scoring 8.5 from 12 reviews. It's a small, clean spot with AC in every room and a range from a budget single bed up to a family room. The in-town location on Charoen Tha Road is a short walk or drive to Wat Phra That and the walking street, making it a good pick for budget travellers who want to stay in town. Real reviews praise the cleanliness and the location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Solo travellers get the cheapest rate with the Standard room; families get better value from the Family room — and the in-town spot means you can walk to Wat Phra That.
pros: Cheapest in the set from just ฿550, AC in every room
In-town location near Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and the walking street
Family room available, good for groups
Small, clean spot — reviews praise the value
cons: Few reviews so far (12) — less data than the others
A small place with simple facilities

entries.name: Huandalha Resort
entries.storyHtml: Huandalha is a garden resort of single-storey rooms set around a garden, in the Pa Sak area near Lamphun town, scoring 7.7 from 19 reviews. The draw is that every room has a kitchenette, fridge and TV — handy for longer stays where you want to cook for yourself — with large rooms and large bathrooms. The Pa Sak location drives into town in a few minutes, making it a good pick for anyone wanting a room with a kitchen on a budget. Real reviews praise the room size and the handy kitchenette.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Staying several nights or want to cook? The in-room kitchenette is the reason to pick this one. Two people travelling together will find the Twin (two beds) more comfortable.
pros: Kitchenette and fridge in every room, good for longer stays
Single-storey rooms around a garden, large rooms and bathrooms
Pa Sak location, quick drive into town
Reviews praise the room size and handy kitchenette
cons: Lowest score in this list at 7.7, with few reviews so far
A simple resort, no pool or big-hotel service

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Lamphun hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Lamphun?
faq.a: It depends on your trip. The walled old town suits temple-walking around Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and the walking street (Pickbaan, BaanKong). Wiang Yong·Mueang Nga, across the Kuang River near town, is the newer-stay zone (Siri, GRAND PA, Nornlamphun, Jamjuree). Pa Sang·Umong·the outskirts suit anyone wanting a quiet garden setting or a base for Chiang Mai too (Look at Home, Suksatan, Loft House).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Lamphun hotels cost?
faq.a: Lamphun stays are mostly budget-friendly: hostels and homestays start around ฿550–900 a night; boutiques and mid-range hotels run about ฿800–1,200; a 4-star resort with a pool starts around ฿1,050 and up. During festivals and the Wat Phra That Hariphunchai fair, prices can rise and rooms fill quickly.

faq.q: ❓ Can I stay in Lamphun and visit Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Easily. It's about a 30–40 minute drive from Lamphun town into Chiang Mai's old city, and roughly 40 minutes from Chiang Mai Airport to Lamphun. Stays around Umong and the Lamphun outskirts (such as Suksatan or Look at Home) are ideal if you want a quiet, budget base for both towns and drive into Chiang Mai for the day.

faq.q: ❓ What is there to see in Lamphun?
faq.a: The in-town highlight is Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, the golden chedi at the town's heart, and Wat Chamthewi. On Friday and Saturday evenings there's the Lamphun walking street. Outside town there are longan orchards, the Wiang Yong silk-weaving village, and several old temples. It's a small town you can walk and drive in a day — great for a stopover or paired with Chiang Mai.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get around Lamphun — do I need to rent a car?
faq.a: Lamphun has no metro and little public transport, so your own car, a motorbike or a rental is the easiest way around, especially if you're staying outside the old town or heading to Umong or Pa Sang. The walled old town is compact enough to walk the temples and the walking street. There are trains and minivans from Chiang Mai to Lamphun for those without a car.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Lamphun hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary by promotion and date, so it's worth comparing all three before you book — each review page in this guide has the comparison links. Many Lamphun stays have limited rooms, so booking ahead helps you get both the price and the room you want.
